notes.decision: Translated 'expelled them forth' from ⲃⲱⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'drive out, expel' (Lyc ⲁ for ⲱ). The verb in this triplet (expel / bind / afflict) is judicial-punitive, fitting the broader narrative of binding the dark powers in the Girdle.
Reduplicated form of ϩⲱϣⲙ̄ 'afflict, oppress' with 3pl suffix. Translated 'afflicted them.' Could also be from ϩⲟϣϩⲱϣ 'crush'; sense is the same — punishment of bound powers.
ⲣⲱⲭⲉ̂ = Lyc ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn'; ⲛ̄ⲥ-ⲧⲉⲕⲟ = infinitive of ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy.' Translated 'burn and destroy.' Distinguished from ⲣ̄ⲱⲭϩ̄ 'consume' (eschatological fire term in glossary).

Translated 'fragrant-breath' from ⲡⲱϣⲙ 'breath, exhalation' + ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrance, sweet odor.' In Manichaean cosmology the soul/spirit's fragrant exhalation is technical. Alternative reading 'incense-worship' (= ϣⲙ̄ϣⲉ-ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ) is possible but less likely given the noun-stem ⲡⲱϣⲙ.
ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓⲧϥ̄ = ⲕⲁⲣⲱⲱⲩ + suffix 'silence, stillness.' Translated 'silence' both here and at line 29.
Lyc reflex of ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'awaken.' Eschatological awakening at the time of the end.

Translated as 'destruction' from Greek ἀναίρεσις 'killing, taking-away, destruction.' The two spellings (with and without -ⲡ-) are scribal variants of the same word. Refers to the eschatological cosmic dissolution. Alternative reading ἀνάπαυσις 'rest' is grammatically possible but contextually inferior — the passage describes the Father scattering forth defilement and gathering light alone, which is destructive-purgative, not restful.
Translated 'encompassing' from ⲕⲱⲛⲥ̄ / ⲕⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'wrap around, embrace, surround.' The First Man encompasses the totality even as he scatters out the foreign defilement.
Translated 'rising-up' from ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise.' The technical complement to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' — here the intransitive nominalized form for the upward motion of light gathered out of all things.
Translated 'this great agony' from ⲁⲣⲱⲛ = Greek ἀγών 'contest, struggle, ordeal.' Standard Manichaean term for the cosmic combat. Lyc ⲣⲱ for ⲅⲱ.

Translated 'there have come to pass the dissolution and the formation' — taking ⲁⲩϩⲉ as past 3pl of ϩⲉ 'fall, happen' with the doublet 'dissolution / formation' as logical subjects. ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'wiping-out, dissolution' (ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ = 'formation, fashioning' — the Manichaean cosmic Image/Statue assembled at the end.

Translated 'hot-stone' tentatively. Etymology unclear; possibly related to ⲱⲃϣ̄/ⲱⲃⲣ ('white-hot iron' or 'glowing implement'), or a specialized term for the heated object dropped into milk to ripen/cook it. The ancient cooking technique of plunging hot stones or irons into milk to thicken/cook it fits perfectly. Flag for review.

ⲥⲟⲩⲱⲧϩ = ⲥⲱⲧϩ 'extract, draw forth, refine.' ⲥⲟⲩⲱϣⲙ̄ⲉ = ⲱϣⲙ̄ 'quench, extinguish.' Together they describe the hot stone's double action in milk: drawing out moisture/essence and quenching its own heat. Standard physical-process pairing.
Greek loanword πέσσειν 'cook, ripen, digest.' The hot stone ripens/cooks the milk. Translated 'ripens.'
